propositions.justification: orders.create_order() has both a db.connection_pool edge and synchronous HTTP edges to auth, inventory, and payment; if the handler keeps a pooled connection while waiting on those downstream calls, slow downstreams can hold all connections.
propositions.predicted_signal: orders POST latency and pool checkout timeouts rise while auth/inventory/payment latency is elevated; active orders pool connections reaches maximum.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() calls auth.verify() synchronously; no graph-level backoff or retry boundary is visible around this cross-service call, so auth verify failures can be retried per order request and amplify load.
propositions.predicted_signal: GET /auth/verify request rate exceeds POST /orders rate during auth failure; retry count per order exceeds 1.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() calls payment.charge() synchronously; without a visible backoff or retry boundary, a slow or failing payment charge can cause order retries to re-hit payment and amplify charge traffic.
propositions.predicted_signal: POST /payment/charge QPS spikes relative to accepted orders; repeated charge attempts for the same order or idempotency key.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() calls inventory.reserve() synchronously; if reserve fails or times out, order retries without graph-visible backoff can repeatedly hit inventory reservation.
propositions.predicted_signal: POST /inventory/{item_id}/reserve QPS spikes after reserve latency or failures; multiple reserve attempts for the same order/item.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() invokes payment.charge(); if POST /orders retries or concurrent duplicate submissions are not guarded by an order-level idempotency key before the downstream charge, the payment idempotency check can still be raced.
propositions.predicted_signal: Multiple payment charge attempts or records for the same order payload or client request identifier.

propositions.justification: payment.charge_payment() invokes payment.check_idempotency(); if the idempotency check and charge commit are not atomic or unique-constrained, concurrent identical charge requests can both pass the check before either records completion.
propositions.predicted_signal: Duplicate charge rows or transactions for a single idempotency key; charge count exceeds unique idempotency key count.

propositions.justification: payment.charge_payment() uses db.connection_pool and invokes check_idempotency, which itself has pool/session edges; nested or long-lived transaction acquisition during concurrent charges can exhaust the pool.
propositions.predicted_signal: payment pool active/checked-out connections saturate; checkout timeout errors on POST /payment/charge under concurrency.

propositions.justification: payment.check_idempotency() queries db.session; without a unique or indexed idempotency key, the lookup can scan or degrade under duplicate retries, making idempotency checks progressively slower.
propositions.predicted_signal: Idempotency lookup time and rows examined rise with charge volume; slow query count on payment idempotency storage.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() reads through db.session for GET /orders; if list pagination computes offset/page boundaries arithmetically, adjacent pages can overlap or skip rows at page boundaries.
propositions.predicted_signal: Consecutive GET /orders pages contain duplicate or missing order_id values; returned counts disagree with page size at boundaries.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() accesses db.session without graph-visible index or pagination constraints; if the handler lazily fetches related order records or scans the orders table for listing, query count or rows scanned scales with result size.
propositions.predicted_signal: DB query count per GET /orders scales with order count/page size; full scans or N+1 query bursts during list requests.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() uses db.connection_pool; slow list queries or N+1 fetches can hold pooled connections for the full response construction, reducing available connections under list traffic.
propositions.predicted_signal: orders connection pool utilization rises with GET /orders concurrency; checkout awaits/timeouts on list requests.

propositions.justification: orders.get_order() reads via db.session; if order detail serialization lazily loads related line items or payments per order, GET /orders/{order_id} exhibits N+1 queries rather than a fixed query count.
propositions.predicted_signal: Per-request DB query count for GET /orders/{order_id} grows with number of related order rows; DB latency scales with detail size.

propositions.justification: orders.get_order() uses db.connection_pool; slow detail queries or N+1 loading can keep connections checked out longer, especially under high detail-read concurrency.
propositions.predicted_signal: orders pool checkout timeouts during GET /orders/{order_id} bursts; active connections track detail endpoint latency.

propositions.justification: inventory.reserve_stock() uses db.connection_pool; stock reservation likely holds row locks or transactions, so contention or slow reservation logic can exhaust the pool under concurrent reservations.
propositions.predicted_signal: inventory pool saturation and lock-wait time increase during concurrent reserve calls; checkout timeouts on POST /inventory/{item_id}/reserve.

propositions.justification: inventory.reserve_stock() accesses db.session without a graph-visible idempotency guard; if POST /inventory/{item_id}/reserve is retried or duplicated concurrently, the same logical reservation can execute more than once.
propositions.predicted_signal: Reserved quantity exceeds requested quantity for the same order/idempotency key; duplicate inventory reservation rows.

propositions.justification: inventory.get_item() accesses db.session; if the item lookup lacks an index on the filter or lazily loads related stock records, GET /inventory/{item_id} can scan or issue N+1 queries.
propositions.predicted_signal: inventory item read latency and rows examined rise with table size; query count per GET /inventory/{item_id} exceeds a constant.

propositions.justification: inventory.get_item() uses db.connection_pool; high item-read volume or a slow scan/N+1 pattern can hold pooled connections and reduce capacity.
propositions.predicted_signal: inventory pool utilization correlates with GET /inventory/{item_id} QPS/latency; checkout timeouts during read bursts.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() calls auth.verify() synchronously; if auth verification is slow or unavailable and orders retries without a visible backoff boundary, GET /auth/verify receives amplified repeated traffic.
propositions.predicted_signal: GET /auth/verify QPS rises above POST /orders QPS during auth failures; repeated verify attempts per order.
